title: The Knowledge of the Reef Edge

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE X: GROWING UP, GROWING OLD AND EVERYDAY JOY (LCJ-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
The rest of the owner's 100 Living Culture ideas and the world-inspired 50: secret languages and forgotten words, coming of age, elders who will not retire, healers' oaths, failed discoveries, masks and clothes and masterpieces nobody wanted, talent shows, ridiculous hats and the day nobody worked.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An elder teaches the signs of dangerous water and the stories in the stars: learn the signs first, or the stories first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) knows every sign of dangerous water: the color of the swell that means a rip, the birds that leave before a storm, the stars that rise before the big tides. (friend) wants to learn it all. (subject) says there are two ways: the signs first, or the stories that hold them. Which way should (friend) learn?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) teaches the signs plainly: this color, this bird, this star. (friend) learns quickly and remembers most of them. The first time (friend.he/she) spots a rip and warns the swimmers, (friend.he/she) is very proud.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) teaches the stories: the star that is a lost fisher, the bird that warned a village. (friend) learns slower, and remembers everything, forever. Years later, (friend.he/she) teaches the stories to (friend.his/her) own children on the beach.
